narrative:
The model predicts a 90% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to depart soon, based on patterns from many similar employees.

The three factors that most influenced this prediction were your overall years of experience, whether you have received other job offers, and how long you have been with this organization. 

Your total professional experience of 6-10 years was the strongest driver pushing the prediction toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have only 1-5 years of experience, your mid-level tenure appears to signal higher mobility in the eyes of the model. The fact that you have received other job opportunities also strongly increased the likelihood of leaving, as having external options often correlates with departure. Finally, your 1-5 years in your current role added further weight toward leaving, since shorter tenure at the present company is more common among those who ultimately move on.

Taken together, these elements created a clear picture of someone ready for change. The organization should consider discussing your career goals with you directly and exploring whether improved recognition, workload balance, or advancement paths could increase your commitment. You may want to reflect on what would make staying worthwhile or whether pursuing those external opportunities aligns with your long-term plans.
